task: Real early Wright-brothers flight film (no 1903 film exists)
subject_box_format: normalised [x0, y0, x1, y1] of the active (pillarboxed) picture inside the 1920x1080 frame

items.title: Wright Brothers' Flight (NARA 16-P-1316-1, NAID 2038)
items.date: 1909-07-27 (catalogue date; Orville Wright's Army acceptance trials at Fort Myer, Virginia)
items.depicts: Silent B&W 16mm film, 1440x1080 picture pillarboxed in a 1920x1080 frame, with burned-in intertitles (later title cards, not 1909 originals). Visible: soldiers pushing the Wright Military Flyer out of its wooden shed and wheeling it to the launching rail; the Flyer on the rail by the derrick (catapult tower); close shots of the two men seated at the controls (intertitle: Orville Wright with passenger Lt. Frank Lahm); crowds and post buildings; the Flyer banking toward the camera over the field, passing low over spectators' heads, cruising above the tree line, a low-level speed run. No clear landing shot. NARA slate 0-6 s; end leader 223-227 s. Audio track is digital silence (-91 dB): no music or narration, no watermark. USABLE RANGES (s, all flight shots are the 1909 Fort Myer trials): 17.0-23.0 soldiers push the Flyer out of the shed; 41.0-47.0 Flyer wheeled across the field past the shed; 77.3-83.0 Flyer on the launching rail, man walks past; 100.5-105.8 close: men seated at the controls (pilot seat, chain drive); 124.6-127.2 catapult tower + Flyer on rail, then short take-off run along the rail (only ~1.4 s of run, 125.8-127.2); 147.0-153.0 BEST: Flyer flies toward camera over the field in front of the tree line and banks, growing larger (a damaged black frame at 153.1 - stop before it); 158.0-162.7 BEST: Flyer passes low over the spectators' heads and away over the barracks; 168.0-172.9 Flyer high over the tree line, passes overhead; 186.8-193.0 Flyer cruising left to right above the tree line, clear silhouette; 212.3-216.9 low-level speed run: Flyer approaches low over the field and banks close past the camera (vertical scratches). Intertitles at ~6-16, 83.1-88.2, 110.7-117.8, 162.9-167.7, 181.8-186.3 (approx.), 204.8-210.1 s - avoid or crop.
items.evidence: NARA catalog NAID 2038, local identifier 16-P-1316-1, title "Wright Brothers' Flight"; scope note: "This film documents the official test flight of the Wright Brothers' military airplane at Fort Myer, Virginia, on July 27, 1909."; date note: "Although this series was created in 1930, this film was produced in 1909."; subjects: Wright, Wilbur, 1867-1912; Wright, Orville, 1871-1948; series 'Public Information and Training Motion Picture and Television Productions' (NAID 1550), Records of the Office of the Secretary of Agriculture (RG 16); Access: Unrestricted; Use: Restricted - Possibly (copyright note). Burned-in intertitles read: "Official Test Flight of Wright Brothers Military Airplane, Fort Myer, July 27, 1909" / "Orville Wright takes his place in the pilot's seat next to his passenger, Lt. Frank Lahm." / "Flight lasts 1 hour and 12 minutes - a world record for a pilot with passenger." CAUTION: two shots (the bank toward camera at 147-153 s, with the same damaged frame, and the pass over spectators) also appear in NARA 111-H-1185, which NARA's Moving Image Lab found (2022, Unwritten Record blog) to splice September 1908 and early-July 1909 footage; so treat individual shots as 'Fort Myer trials, 1908-1909' rather than certainly 27 July 1909. Not 1903 and not Kitty Hawk.
items.licence: Public domain in the US (no known copyright): 1909 footage held in US Department of Agriculture motion-picture records (NARA RG 16), i.e. a US federal-agency film (17 U.S.C. 105), and in any case created/published more than 115 years ago. NARA catalog fields: Access 'Unrestricted'; Use 'Restricted - Possibly' (generic note: 'Some or all of this material may be restricted by copyright or other intellectual property rights and restrictions.' - no rights holder named). NARA does not print an explicit 'public domain' statement on this record.

items.title: First Army Aeroplane Flight, Fort Myer, Virginia (NARA 111-H-1185, NAID 24690)
items.date: 1908-09 and 1909-07 (Fort Myer trials; compiled by the Signal Corps in 1935-36)
items.depicts: Silent B&W 35mm film, ~1500x1078 picture pillarboxed in a 1920x1080 frame, no intertitles; NARA slate 0-6 s and 'End of Recording' card 471.7-474.7 s. Audio track is digital silence (-91 dB): no music, narration or watermark. Some shots have mould/reticulation texture in the sky (esp. 395-430 s) and a few damaged frames. Visible: officers and dignitaries at the shed doors; soldiers remove the shed doors and push the Wright Military Flyer out; Flyer wheeled across the parade ground with the Fort Myer post buildings behind; close shots of the men in the seats; men at the catapult derrick; take-off along the rail; many flight shots (toward camera, over the tree line, over spectators, over the barracks, a cavalryman on horseback in frame); the Flyer at rest on the field after landing; crowd and officers around it; close-up of the engine/chain drive and seats. USABLE RANGES (s): 100.0-106.0 soldiers and officers with the Flyer at the shed; 165.0-171.5 soldiers wheel the Flyer across the field, post buildings behind; 175.8-181.0 close: man climbing into / seated at the controls; 229.6-232.6 catapult derrick weight drops and the Flyer runs along the rail (take-off; NARA notes this take-off is spliced from 1908 and 1909 footage, two different aircraft); 254.6-258.5 BEST: Flyer flies toward camera over the field and banks (single damaged black frame at ~258.56 - end before it, or resume 258.6-260.6); 289.6-295.6 BEST: Flyer approaches above the tree line, banks and passes overhead large; 320.2-325.8 Flyer cruising above the tree line; 327.6-331.4 BEST: very low pass overhead, both men visible in silhouette, camera pans over the post buildings and crowd (327.3 has a ghosted frame - start after it); 366.0-370.4 Flyer skims over the tree line low and passes overhead out of frame; 373.9-378.0 Flyer passes over spectators' heads and away over the barracks; 413.8-418.0 Flyer banks close above spectators (heavy mottled texture in sky); 445.0-451.0 Flyer at rest on the field after the flight, men walking up (dark); 457.0-463.0 officers and soldiers crowd around the landed Flyer; 466.6-471.0 close-up of the Flyer's engine, chain drive and seats. No usable landing touchdown (only ~2 s, tiny, at 442.7-444.8).
items.evidence: NARA catalog NAID 24690, local identifier 111-H-1185, title "First Army Aeroplane Flight" (other title 'Historical Film'), series 'Historical Films' (NAID 24608), creator War Department. Office of the Chief Signal Officer, Records of the Office of the Chief Signal Officer (RG 111). Scope note: "This film includes footage of Orville Wright and Lt. Frank P. Lahm, the first Army passenger, testing the 'Wright Flyer' during trials at Fort Myer, Virginia. Notable dignitaries present include President and Mrs. Taft, Major Squier, Major Saltzman. Wright and Lahm set the world's endurance record of one hour 12 minutes and 40 seconds." Online-resource note: "In September of 2022 the Moving Image Lab at the National Archives at College Park, MD authenticated the date of footage for National Archives Identifier 24690, Local Identifier 111-H-1185 ... making this the oldest government film in the holdings of the National Archives." NARA Unwritten Record blog (2022-09-01): tests were first held at Fort Myer in September 1908; the film also contains scenes from the beginning of July 1909; the Signal Corps combined 1908 and 1909 footage so the take-off looks like one launch (two different planes); USDA employee Winfield Scott Clime is named as the 1908 cameraman. Production file (War Department, Office of the Chief Signal Officer, Photographic Division, 1936; saved as production_file.pdf) lists 23 scenes, 675 ft, e.g. 'Scene 8. Mr. Wright gets into plane', 'Scene 13. Long shot - taking off', 'Scene 20. Plane landing', 'Scene 23. Mr. Wright getting out of plane'. Pilot is Orville Wright (Wilbur was in France in 1908 and did not fly at Fort Myer). Not 1903 and not Kitty Hawk; label as 'Fort Myer, Virginia, 1908-1909'.
items.licence: Public domain in the US (no known copyright): US Army Signal Corps (War Department, Office of the Chief Signal Officer) 'Historical Films' compilation (NARA RG 111) of 1908-1909 footage; NARA calls it 'the oldest government film' in its holdings and names a USDA employee (Winfield Scott Clime) as the 1908 cameraman, i.e. a US federal-government work (17 U.S.C. 105), and in any case created more than 115 years ago. NARA catalog fields: Access 'Unrestricted'; Use 'Restricted - Possibly' (generic copyright note, no rights holder named). NARA does not print an explicit 'public domain' statement on this record.
